status_reason: the gating targets (balanced naive OCT vs MCH choice; naive avoidance of each odour vs air) are standard but their published values were NOT read (Tully & Quinn 1985 paywalled; Li 2013 Fig. 1I not extracted). A library check must fill them before preregistration.
summary: Naive T-maze choice at the choice point, before any learning: OCT vs MCH should be balanced, and each odour vs air should be avoided.

stimulus.design: one fly at the choice point, arm A left and arm B right, then reciprocal (swapped); relative concentration 1 = the DoOR consensus scale
stimulus.literature_match: T-maze: ~100 flies per trial, reciprocal half-PIs (Li 2013 methods); OCT 1.5e-3 and MCH 1e-3 v/v there. The body and the maze geometry are not simulated (roadmap P2/P3).

encoder.default_spontaneous_basis: median of the Hallem 2006 spontaneous rates of 24 Ors (1.0-47.0 Hz), for glomeruli without a Hallem value
encoder.r_max_basis: engineering scale for DoOR (0-1 per receptor): Hallem 2004 via DoOR gives 245 spikes/s for Or85b to OCT; not a fitted value
encoder.contralateral_basis: declared design choice: maximal lateralisation at the choice point; no verified value
encoder.rate_to_drive: validation.paradigms.tmaze_odor.drive_for_rate: inverse of the resting LIF rate for the declared engine constants
encoder.table_source: validation/specs/sources/door2_orn_responses_oct_mch_bza.json (DoOR.data db323a4). Units with no single glomerulus dropped; duplicate units in one glomerulus averaged; a missing odour entry means no DoOR data and is treated as no evoked response.

decoder.rule: choice = side with more DNa02 spikes over the decision window (ipsilateral steering); tie = no choice, excluded from the PI

seed_role: encoder per-cell noise; each seed is one fly tested in both side assignments

analysis.PI: PI(a) = (choices of a - choices of b) / choosers, resampled by seed

gates.claim: More than half the trials end in a choice (otherwise the PI is not informative).
gates.basis: design precondition; not a literature value

gates.claim: Naive OCT vs MCH choice is balanced: PI 95% CI inside [-0.2, 0.2].
gates.basis: standard: odour concentrations are set so naive flies split evenly (Tully & Quinn 1985); the tolerance is a judgement

gates.claim: Naive flies avoid OCT against air (PI for OCT below 0).
gates.basis: naive odour avoidance is measured against air as a control in T-maze work (Li 2013 methods); values not read

gates.claim: Naive flies avoid MCH against air.

decision_rule: Behaviour PASS iff every gate passes. Physiology PASS iff every check lies in its bound. Verdict PASS iff both pass on a confirmatory run (real graph, this spec committed and unchanged, these seeds, clean tree); PASS_PROVISIONAL if any gating value is marked unverified; FAIL if any gate or check fails; INCONCLUSIVE if one cannot be evaluated. Full rule: validation/harness.py VERDICTS.

tully1985.citation: Tully T, Quinn WG (1985) Classical conditioning and retention in normal and mutant Drosophila melanogaster. J Comp Physiol A 157:263-277

li2013.citation: Li W, et al. (2013) J Neurosci (T-maze methods: naive odour avoidance, reciprocal half-PIs)
li2013.read: methods only; control values are in Fig. 1I and were NOT extracted
values_read: ~100 flies per trial; MCH 1e-3 v/v, OCT 1.5e-3 v/v; half-PI = (n_air - n_odour)/total, PI = mean of reciprocal half-PIs

munch2016.citation: Münch D, Galizia CG (2016) DoOR 2.0 - Comprehensive mapping of Drosophila melanogaster odorant responses. Sci Rep 6:21841
values_read: consensus responses (0-1 per receptor, spontaneous-subtracted as reset_sfr does) for 3-octanol and 4-methylcyclohexanol; receptor -> glomerulus mapping (sources/door2_orn_responses_oct_mch_bza.json)

hallem2006.citation: Hallem EA, Carlson JR (2006) Coding of odors by a receptor repertoire. Cell 125:143-160
hallem2006.doi_status: matches DoOR.data records; not resolved online
values_read: spontaneous firing of 24 Ors in the empty-neuron system, 1-47 Hz (SFR row)
OCT and MCH were NOT in the 110-odour set

rayshubskiy2025.citation: Rayshubskiy A, et al., Wilson RI (2025) eLife 13:RP102230 (preprint bioRxiv 2020.04.04.024703)
rayshubskiy2025.read: text; no absolute DNa02 firing rates in the text (figures only)
